Subject: SEV-1 / SEV-2: Platform latency impacting Edgeware — bridge coordination & executive update

Team — Michael/Sara, quick note to confirm we’re fully engaged on this. We have declared a SEV-1 for the generation latency/timeout cluster impacting your production region and have an active engineering bridge running.

What we’ve done so far:
- Triage: SRE team has identified abnormal GPU queueing and increased retry rates on the inference tier.
- Mitigation: Traffic has been routed to backup capacity where available; we’ve applied temporary rate limiting on long-running requests.
- Bridge: Live bridge established (Zoom: https://zoom.us/j/1234567890).

Immediate ask: Can you confirm the most impacted services on your side and any queued jobs we should deprioritize while we stabilize?

I’ll run this bridge and provide rolling executive updates every 60–90 minutes until we have a stable recovery. Attaching a one-page snapshot for your ops and the current bridge notes.

Attachments: [status_snapshot_v1.pdf (PDF, 245 KB)], [bridge_notes.txt (TXT)]

—
Marissa Cole

Subject: RE: SEV-1 / SEV-2: Platform latency impacting Edgeware — internal note

Internal status update (do not forward to customer).
- Root cause hypothesis: intermittent GC+kernel contention on a subset of the A100 fleet in us-west-2 causing request spikes and queue saturation.
- Short-term plan: throttle background eval/bench traffic, fail-fast on requests exceeding 8s, and shift affected shards to warm standby nodes.
- ETA for visible improvement: we expect a measurable latency reduction within ~18–30 minutes after throttles and shard shifts complete.
- Action: Jonas to coordinate shard promotion and I’ll run the fail-fast rollout.

Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Michael Turner <m.turner@edgeware.io>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com, ethan_park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 4 Nov 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident follow-up: Edgeware SEV-1 (timeline, root cause, next steps)

Michael/Sara — thank you for your partnership during the bridge. Below is the initial follow-up and draft postmortem. We’ll schedule a walk-through with your team and your CFO as requested.

Summary (short):
- Incident window: 2025-11-03T15:07:00Z — 2025-11-03T18:35:00Z (approx).
- Impact: Elevated 95/99 latency for generation APIs in us-west-2; intermittent request timeouts and retries; Edgeware observed backlog of ~12k queued jobs.
- Root cause (initial): A combination of an out-of-step kernel update on a subset of inference hosts and uncontrolled background evaluation traffic caused GPU resource contention and queue growth.
- Immediate mitigations applied: forced fail-fast on long-running requests, throttling of background evals, shard promotion to standby nodes, and rolling rollback of the problematic kernel build.
- Current status: Service recovered to baseline by ~2025-11-03T18:35:00Z after mitigations; monitoring is green and we have a verification window running.

Customer impact and financial sensitivity: we recognize this affected an ordered job stream for Edgeware that is revenue-affecting. Marissa will be your point for SLA credit coordination and exec engagement. I’ve also attached the draft postmortem and the bridge notes for your review.

Planned follow-ups:
- Internal: durable mitigations to prevent accidental kernel rollouts to inference fleets without canary windows (owner: infra team).
- Product: rate-limit guardrails for background evals and a preemption mechanism for customer-critical jobs (owner: runtime/product).
- Ops: improve cross-region failover playbook and add clearer progressive rollback steps (owner: SRE).

Action items for Edgeware (optional): share any correlate logs or request-IDs you want included in the postmortem verification block; we’ll incorporate them into the final doc.

Attachments: [postmortem-draft-Edgeware-20251104.md (MD, 18 KB)]

Next step: Marissa will follow up this afternoon with a compact executive one-pager for your CFO and schedule a joint postmortem review for next week (suggested: Tue 2025-11-11).

Regards,
